hero.headline: Port St. Lucie City Council to vote Monday on Tradition commercial rezoning near Crosstown Parkway
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council is scheduled to hold a second reading and final vote Monday on a proposed land use change in Tradition that would convert nearly 9.5 acres near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive from residential to commercial designation. Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo, who live along the edge of the property, have voiced concerns about how future development could alter the character of the community they moved to call home. Joseph Mucciolo told WPTV two months ago that he feared the change could force his family to move, saying if these things come to pass, they may seek other grounds and other places to go.

The request, submitted by Winding River Crosstown, LLC, would amend the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development plan by removing the property from residential designation and creating a new parcel designated for retail and office uses. The city says the change would allow for future commercial development on the site, but any future project would still need to go through additional review and approval processes. For the Mucciolos, the concern is not only what could be built but how it could change the feel of their neighborhood.

The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the amendment with conditions in May. Those conditions include a 10-foot enhanced landscape buffer and architectural wall along portions of the property bordering residential areas, requirements to limit lighting impacts, and eliminating a possible future connection to SW Glenbrook Drive. Joseph Mucciolo said this is their backyard and where they spend the majority of their day. He expressed concern that the open space is going to be gone, and if they put up a wall it is going to look like a prison.

Margaret Mucciolo said the family worries losing the open space behind their home could impact the quality of life they value. She said they do not want over development and want city leaders to consider their concerns before making a final decision. The proposal now returns to city council for what could be a final vote on the land use change.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: TCCEED doubles employer participation in second year of paid summer internship program
cards.teaser: The Treasure Coast workforce development program placed 61 students in local jobs this summer while tripling the number of applications from area students.
cards.body:
TCCEED expanded its paid summer internship program in its second year, doubling employer participation and placing 61 students in local jobs across the Treasure Coast. The initiative also saw applications from Treasure Coast students triple compared to the previous year.

The program connects local high school and college students with paid internship opportunities at businesses throughout Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. TCCEED partners with employers to create meaningful work experiences while providing students with income and professional development opportunities during summer break.

cards.headline: World Cup semifinals set as England and Argentina advance to final four
cards.teaser: England beat Norway behind two goals from Jude Bellingham, while Argentina defeated Switzerland with a Julian Alvarez extra-time strike to reach the semifinals.
cards.body:
The World Cup semifinal matchups are complete after England and Argentina advanced through the quarterfinals over the weekend. England defeated Norway with Jude Bellingham scoring twice to inspire his team past Erling Haaland's Norway. Argentina relied on Julian Alvarez, who scored in extra time to help the team through to the semifinal with assistance from a controversial VAR call.

The four highest-ranked teams in the world reached the semifinals. Both Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored six goals in the competition, and England has relied on these two superstars to avoid elimination. Argentina has scored the most goals of anyone in the competition with 17 and has the added bonus of experience, with many members of the current squad winning the title in 2022.

France faces Spain in one semifinal, while England takes on Argentina in the other. France has been considered the tournament favorite and is supported by Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele and a host of other talented attackers. Spain has conceded just one goal the entire tournament and beat France in the Euro 2024 semifinals and the Nations League last year. The semifinals begin Tuesday, with the final scheduled for July 19.

cards.headline: Linda Noskova wins Wimbledon women's title after recovering from five blown match points
cards.teaser: The 21-year-old Czech player defeated Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final for her first Grand Slam trophy.
cards.body:
Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. The 21-year-old became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth.

Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance, as was Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club. Navratilova looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Lightning strike ignites one of two Martin County brush fires this week
cards.teaser: Martin County experienced two brush fires this week, with lightning causing at least one of the blazes.
cards.body:
Martin County experienced two brush fires this week, with lightning causing at least one of the blazes. Both fires are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the department, said this is their peak season for such fires. He explained that the summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them receptive and ready to ignite. When lightning strikes these dried fuels, fires start quickly. Grubitch said rain often extinguishes these fires immediately, but sometimes they travel underground and surface days later.

The Florida Forest Service says the conditions that fuel these fires are not going away anytime soon, but residents should not be alarmed. The combination of summer heat and dry vegetation creates an environment where fires can easily ignite, particularly during thunderstorms when lightning strikes are common. While the two fires this week have been contained, officials continue to monitor the situation as weather conditions remain favorable for additional brush fires.

Grubitch said the public plays a crucial role in helping the Florida Forest Service do its job. He stressed that residents should never assume someone else has already called in a brush fire, saying that if you see something, say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control. Quick reporting allows firefighters to respond faster and prevent small fires from spreading into larger, more dangerous blazes that threaten homes and property.

cards.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with 105-step climb to panoramic views
cards.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, offers visitors a 105-step climb to panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
cards.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse stands as a 165-year-old sentinel on Florida's Atlantic coast, where its red brick tower has guided mariners since 1860. Built at the base of the Jupiter Inlet, the lighthouse continues to function as an active navigational aid while welcoming visitors who want to explore its history and experience the views from its observation gallery. The structure has served continuously as a beacon for ships navigating the coastal waters, maintaining its original purpose while also opening its doors to the public.

Reaching the top of the lighthouse requires climbing 105 steps up a narrow spiral staircase that winds through the interior of the brick tower. This is the same route that lighthouse keepers climbed night after night throughout history to maintain the powerful Fresnel lens that projected light across the water. The spiral staircase follows the path of these early keepers who ensured the beacon remained operational for passing ships. The climb takes visitors upward through the tower to the gallery that sits at the top of the structure.

The observation gallery provides panoramic views that stretch across multiple waterways and the ocean. The Atlantic Ocean extends to the east, while below the tower, the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet converge with the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers. Visitors standing at the elevated vantage point can watch boats glide through the channel as sea breezes sweep across the observation area. The commanding perspective reveals why this particular location proved ideal for a lighthouse, offering clear sightlines across the coastal landscape and waterways.

The museum grounds preserve more than just the tower itself. Restored historic buildings chronicle the lighthouse's journey from its construction before the Civil War through its years as an active Coast Guard station. These structures provide information about the lighthouse's role in regional maritime history and offer details about the daily lives of the keepers who operated the station. The site maintains the supporting buildings that allowed the lighthouse station to function across more than a century and a half of continuous service, preserving the complete story of this working navigational aid that has marked the Florida coastline for generations of mariners.
